text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing memory creep on staging streaming-chat when tool loops run long (~30k tokens). KV slab allocations climb and don’t reclaim after session end. Repro: toolchain T3 on staging-gpu-pool. Anyone seen this?

devin: Hmm, saw similar on dedicated-rw-8 yesterday. Did the kernel-selection/alignment PR land on main recently? @liam

liam: Yeah, that PR modified kernel selection heuristics for short vs long seqs (commit e3f4b9d) and adjusted slab alignment 64->128 to try to improve cache locality. Could be a side-effect.

rachel: Collected perf traces and a flamegraph: https://perf.internal/reports/2026/2026504321-kv-slab.svg 
Key note from the profile: `kv_slab_alloc` steady +1.2MB/sec across session window. Heap shows many small live refs in `page_bucket_3`.

perf-bot: Alert: kv-cache-residency increased by 48% on staging at 2026-02-18T15:12Z. Trace id: abcd-1234.

maya: I pulled `/admin/kv/inspect` for session `0x7fa`: ```alloc_map: {shard0: 142M, shard1: 139M, free_chunks: 12} eviction_candidates: []``` — eviction_candidates empty despite clear mem pressure.

devin: Can you run `./tools/kv_eviction_probe --session 0x7fa --run-evict`? It forces eviction and prints reasons + fragmentation stats.

maya: Ran it. Freed ~62MB but fragmentation persists. Output: `freed 62MB, fragmented: 18 chunks (avg 2KB), largest_free_contig=8KB`.

liam: That aligns with an aliasing/fragmentation hypothesis — increasing alignment to 128B can inflate internal fragmentation so large contiguous pages become scarce. Need to check the page_coalescer logic and whether it coalesces across slab boundaries.

rachel: Also observed duplicate prefix writes from streaming tool loop where metadata toggles slightly (trace id appended). Example: `put(key=conv:123:prefix:hash(0x1a), meta=ctx_v2)` vs `put(... meta=ctx_v2+trace)` — causing multiple near-duplicates pinned in KV.

sre-oncall: Is this leading to OOMs in staging? Any customer-facing impact?

maya: Staging OOMs in long-run smoke; no prod reports yet. Repro config attached in thread.

devin: Mitigation I can push now: enable `kv.force_coalesce=true` and lower `kv.max_slab_alloc` on staging to force more aggressive coalescing and cap slab growth.

liam: Long-term options: revert alignment change, or enhance coalescer to merge adjacent free chunks across the new alignment boundaries and add tests to simulate chunk aliasing patterns.

rachel: I'll add a perf regression test that runs the tool-loop harness for 6+ hrs and records slab metrics + fragmentation histograms. Assigning to me for follow-up. @devin can you apply the staging flag?

devin: On it. Pushing staging flag via admin endpoint: `curl -XPOST https://staging-admin.internal/flags -d '{"kv.force_coalesce":true,"kv.max_slab_alloc":"256MB"}'`

maya: :thumbsup: I'll rerun the long-run after change and post results.

perf-bot: Change detected: kv.force_coalesce=true applied to staging at 2026-02-18T15:35Z.

maya: Post-change results: memory growth rate dropped to ~0.2MB/sec and no OOM in a 6h run. Fragmentation still visible but much reduced. Posting logs.

liam: Great. Please file a bug and set P1 if reproduced in prod. Suggested follow-ups: (1) reproduce with allocator alignment toggles (64/128), (2) add coalescer unit tests + fuzz for near-duplicate keys, (3) add telemetry exposing chunk size distribution & aliasing rate.

devin: Filed BUG-2026-118 `kv-slab-aliasing-fragmentation` with repro steps and attached perf traces.

maya: Thanks — will keep monitoring long-run jobs and post any anomalies. :eyes:
